answer.rationale:
The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and the strongest inherited evidence for that stage is memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) reinforced by memory_31 (signup field reduction produced a durable SMB activation lift). Because that is the direction I intend to commit to, I am spending verification budget on those two rather than on memories I do not plan to act on: memory_86 to confirm the effect size and whether it was measured on the same self-serve population now under competitive pressure, and memory_31 because at day 12 it is the oldest record here and a 'durable lift' claim measured that early may not have had time to be durable.

I am deliberately not selecting promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing making it the emotionally obvious counter. Memory_73 carries its own caveat: the 31% conversion and 18% revenue gains came with a 12-point later-cycle retention loss and an explicit instruction not to treat it as a repeatable win. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that memory is evidence against the action, not for it, and I am carrying the caveat forward rather than quoting only the headline number. Matching a price war on a competitor's terms would also likely buy the least loyal segment.

Downstream value risk: if simplified onboarding works by removing qualifying fields, it can raise activation counts while lowering lead quality and feeding weaker accounts to sales — the same shape of harm as memory_73, just measured later. I will instrument on downstream qualified revenue and retention cohorts, not on completion rate alone, so a hollow win is detectable.

Uncertainty I am preserving: memory_86 and memory_31 both describe gains from a healthier baseline; the current decline may be caused by competitive churn or segment mix rather than by onboarding friction, in which case reducing friction addresses a symptom. Memory_91 (activation messaging) is the live alternative and stays queued for the next slot. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) both look sound but target segments not currently regressing, so they are lower priority this week. Standard experiment scale, not broad rollout, because the supporting records predate the current competitive conditions.
